messages:
Alex: heads up — we need a quick sync on the proposed telemetry shape change for console metrics. plan is to coerce some routed_count fields from int -> float to support fractional sampling, and to reshard route_id space with a new 64-bit salt. wondering about backfill strategy and dashboard continuity.
Maria: thanks. high level: coercion is fine but will break equality joins in some analytics queries. A few questions: 1) do we keep old int field around (route_count_int) for a grace window? 2) how long is dual-write?
Jon: +1 keep old field. For backfills we can populate the new float field from historical ints easily. bigger problem is the reshard: queries that relied on top-k per shard will change distribution. dashboards using group_by shard_bucket will need migration.
Sarah: from console side, we care about continuity for per-route SLA widgets. If the aggregation keys change we must map old route_id -> new_shard in the UI layer, otherwise users will see spikes. prefer an adapter layer in the console to mask change for 2w.
Kyle: infra note — schema migration that alters shard key will require rolling indexing and a coordinated swap. plan suggestion: dual-write to v1 and v2, expose a feature-flagged read path to query v2 only after backfill completes. We'll run a shadow backfill job with throttling.
Alex: ok dual-write + adapter sounds good. What about quota evaluation — we currently use integer token counts to evaluate quota buckets. fractional counts will change bucket boundaries slightly. Do we recompute quota windows?
Maria: for quota evaluation we should keep quota calculus in integers for now. Implement: emit fractional telemetry for analytics only, and have a deterministic binning function that maps fractional tokens -> integer quota units. That avoids changing billing logic mid-rollout.
Jon: agree. Implementation detail: telemetry proto change adds field `token_fractional` (double) and keeps `token_count` (int64). Backfill sets token_fractional = token_count. For sharding, add `shard_salt_v2` metadata.
Sarah: UX rollout plan: 1) console flags to opt-in display of v2 metrics, 2) default to v1 for 7 days post-backfill, 3) automated diff telemetry to show any >1% divergence per-route before flip.
Kyle: ops checklist draft: - create new index on analytics.v2 (shard_salt_v2) - dual-write API change behind flag - run backfill with low-iops window overnight - run a small canary of 1000 routes - flip reads for canary and monitor - widen canary if diffs <1% - final flip. Also prepare rollback steps (truncate v2 if needed).
Alex: sounds good. wondering about query compatibility: should we provide a SQL view that unifies v1/v2 for dashboards (so dashboard SQLs don't change)?
Jon: yes, create a read-view `analytics.current_metrics` that coalesces fields and exposes route_id canonical. Under the hood it selects from v2 if present else v1. Performance caveat though — views can be slow. We might materialize the view for high-cardinality dashboards.
Maria: perf note: materialized view maintenance will add cost. alternative: let console query v2 via the adapter and keep v1 for billing reads. Then dashboards with heavy queries can point to a materialized table maintained by the backfill job.
Sarah: we should document all of this in the rollout doc and add an in-console notice for customers using SLA widgets. I'll draft the UX copy.
Kyle: also add alerting: if any route shows >5% token divergence after backfill, auto-rollback for that route's reading to v1 and notify #incidents.
Alex: ok action items: Maria to draft proto + dual-write patch, Jon to sketch backfill job and view/materialization plan, Kyle to prepare infra checklist and alerts, Sarah to draft UX messaging and console adapter spec. I'll own coordinating canary.
Maria: working on proto diff now, will post link.
DevBot: deploybot: created a feature-flag "telemetry_v2_dualwrite" (off) for eng-platform.
Alex: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10am to finalize canary targets.
